title: Cancelling tasks and cutting off recursion

questions.stem: Per this page, what does `cancel(true)` do to a ForkJoinTask that is already running?

options.text: It interrupts the worker thread, since true asks for an interrupt while it runs
options.says: The page says that for a ForkJoinTask a task that is already running is not interrupted.

options.text: It does not interrupt the task, since here the argument has no effect at all
options.says: The page says for a ForkJoinTask the argument has no effect: a task that is already running is not interrupted.

options.text: It does not interrupt the task, since only cancel(false) sends such an interrupt
options.says: The page says for a ForkJoinTask the argument has no effect, so neither true nor false leads to an interrupt.

questions.stem: Per this page, what goes wrong when a fork/join Fibonacci task uses a sequential cutoff well below 20?

options.text: The task count grows exponentially, so creating and scheduling tasks dominates
options.says: The page's pitfall 5 says naive recursive Fibonacci creates an exponential number of tasks, and Q5 says too many tasks bring excessive creation and scheduling overhead.

options.text: The task count stays too low, so some of the cores are left sitting idle
options.says: The page's Q5 ties too few tasks and idle cores to a large threshold; a small threshold gives too many tasks.

options.text: The recursion tree gets shallower, so each leaf task does more of the work
options.says: The page's Q5 gives depth as ceil(log2(N / T)), so a smaller threshold makes the tree deeper, not shallower.
